contributions: Systematic comparison of LLM-GNN integration strategies (LLM-as-encoder, TAPE, LLM-as-reasoner, joint training)
Coverage of graph instruction tuning frameworks (InstructGLM, GraphGPT)
Introduction of graph foundation models (PRODIGY via prompt graphs, OFA via shared text space)
Empirical benchmarking on ogbn-arxiv showing progressive accuracy gains from BoW baseline (71.7%) to OFA (78.0%)
limitations: LLM-as-encoder cannot adjust representations to account for structural signals since the LLM is frozen
LLM-as-reasoner struggles with structural reasoning beyond a few hops, is constrained by context windows, and may hallucinate structural relationships
Feature space heterogeneity: no shared vocabulary across graph domains (different dimensionalities, modalities)
Task heterogeneity: different graph tasks require different output heads and loss functions
Structural diversity: models trained on one graph topology may not transfer to another

Graph instruction tuning requires (instruction, graph description, response) triples that are harder to collect than (graph, label) pairs, limiting it to domains like citation networks and knowledge bases
Joint fine-tuning and OFA require substantial GPU resources for 7B+ parameter models
Production API costs and latency for per-query LLM calls are not reflected in benchmark accuracy figures
methods: The chapter describes multiple architectural strategies for combining LLMs and GNNs on text-attributed graphs. Strategy 1 uses a frozen LLM as an offline feature extractor, feeding BERT embeddings into a GCN. Strategy 2 (TAPE) uses an LLM to generate soft pseudo-labels and explanations for unlabeled nodes as additional supervision. Strategy 3 prompts an LLM directly with natural-language descriptions of graph neighborhoods for zero-shot classification. Joint training (GraphGPT, OFA) fine-tunes both components end-to-end. PRODIGY trains a backbone GNN on diverse graphs and uses prompt graphs with labeled examples for in-context learning at inference. OFA projects all node features into a shared natural-language space via an LLM encoder before GNN processing.
results: On ogbn-arxiv (170K nodes, 40 classes), GCN+BoW achieves 71.7% test accuracy. GCN+frozen BERT reaches 73.5%. TAPE with GPT-3.5 achieves 76.5%. InstructGLM (LLaMA-7B) reaches 76.9%. GraphGPT (Vicuna-7B) reaches 77.2%. OFA (LLaMA-7B) achieves 78.0%. The general accuracy gains across strategies are summarized as: LLM-as-encoder +2-4%, TAPE +4-6%, LLM-as-reasoner +0-3%, joint LLM-GNN +6-10% over BoW.
tldr: This chapter surveys three LLM+GNN integration strategies—LLM-as-encoder, TAPE pseudo-labels, and joint fine-tuning/graph instruction tuning—for text-attributed graphs, and introduces graph foundation models (PRODIGY, OFA) that enable cross-dataset transfer.
